narrative.overview: Slabs is a working drawing, not a dashboard. The page is drafting paper, the lines are ink, and the plan is marked the way a carpenter marks boards before sawing: chalk lines for plate joints, a start tick with an arrow for each start point, a pencil X through waste, a circled dot for the face side, a dashed fold where a board bends.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-and-ink palette; colour only for meaning
Marks that double as the legend of the whole interface
Tabular figures everywhere numbers are compared
Dense but never cramped: 44 px targets, 1 px rules
Every state explained in words next to its mark

rules.name: The Colour-Is-Meaning Rule
rules.body: A colour that does not answer "what is this?" is removed.

rules.name: The Not-By-Colour-Alone Rule
rules.body: Every colour has a second carrier: a shape, a pattern, a word or a mark.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Numbers that are compared sit in tabular figures.

rules.name: The 12-Pixel Floor
rules.body: Text in drawings is never smaller than 12 px; a larger drawing scrolls in its frame instead.

rules.name: The Flat-On-Paper Rule
rules.body: Nothing at rest casts a shadow; only floating things do.

dos: Do mark every measured thing with a dimension line and its figure
Do give every colour a second carrier
Do keep text in drawings at 12 px or more
Do keep controls at 44 px or more
Do show a stale result dimmed with "Nieaktualne – przelicz"
donts: Don't use grey CAD canvases, toolbar chrome, wood textures, or saw icons
Don't put a card around every block or build rows of metric tiles
Don't use text glyphs for icons
Don't use red for room names
Don't draw plates for a plan that cannot be built
